lessonPlan.topic: Student Book p.25 - A Listen, point, and say

details:
Listen, point, and say checks understanding of word meaning and sound.
Listen and point shows students can match what they hear to the right image. 
Say practises first-step pronunciation.
Look for careful listening, correct pointing, clear sounds, and confident repetition.
“I love visiting the farm shop but I keep forgetting what to buy! Can you help me with my shopping list?”

Heads Up: 
Focus the students’ attention on the CPT and present relevant features of the language (MFP). Then demonstrate the activity with TA/students.
Heads Down: 
Ss open their books. Instruct and ask ICQs. Then monitor, providing support and stretch where needed. Conduct activity feedback and error correction.
Heads Together: 
Demo/Instruct and ask ICQs, including setting behaviour expectations. Then monitor, providing support and stretch where needed. Conduct activity feedback and error correction.
Reward moment
Check behaviour expectations and reward with APOS or remind for 4Rs

lessonPlan.topic: Student Book p.25 - B. Listen and circle

details: Listen and circle continues checking sound–image connections. Students listen for specific words, then show understanding by circling the correct picture.
Look for careful listening, accurate choices, clear circling, and neat work in students’ books.
“Thanks for coming with me to the shop! I just need one more thing. Can you help me work out what it is?”

lessonPlan.topic: Activity Book p.77 - A Look and connect

details: Look and connect helps students with spelling and matching skills as they connect each letter to make the name of a fruit or vegetable.
Look for accurate work, correct connections between letters and a good understanding of the task.
“When we were at the farm shop, I told the shopkeeper we would help make some new signs for her shop. Can you order these letters to make the signs?

Focus the students’ attention on the CPT and present relevant features of the language (MFP). Then demonstrate the activity with TA/students.
Heads Down: 
Ss open their books. Instruct and ask ICQs. Then monitor, providing support and stretch where needed. Conduct activity feedback and error correction.

lessonPlan.topic: Activity Book p.77 - B Look and write

details: Look and write builds writing accuracy and careful copying through reading and writing. It allows students to learn key vocabulary too.
Look for correct recognition of visuals as they write their answers and neat handwriting with use of the lines provided.

lessonPlan.topic: Student Book p.26 - C. Ask and answer

details: Ask and answer gives students the opportunity to practice using the target language to ask and respond to simple questions.
Look for use of fruit and vegetable vocabulary and ensure students are taking turns and using the picture prompts to help them,
“Now we’re home from the shop, it’s time to put all the food away. Apples, oranges and bananas go in the fruit bowl. Potatoes, onions and carrots in the vegetable box. Will you help?”

lessonPlan.topic: Student Book p.26 - D. Ask and answer

details: Ask and answer develops speaking fluency by allowing students to practise target language using a simple question and answer format.
Look for students using the correct question forms, giving clear answers and taking turns during their short conversations.
“Time to cook a nice vegetable stew and a fruit smoothie, using all of our shopping. Can you help me cut up everything we need?

Read, listen and say provides the opportunity to use the target structure and vocabulary in a chant, as well as practising listening and reading skills.
Look for accurate reading, good pronunciation as they follow the lyrics.
“That is delicious - well done!. Let’s sing a fun chant together to celebrate!”

Heads Up (Reading): 
Focus the students’ attention on the CPT and help Ss to understand the text by asking questions, practicing skimming (reading for gist), scanning (reading for specific information) and detail (reading for comprehension). Then demonstrate the activity with TA/students.
